title: 第10章 违背常识的奇迹第9章 你想要什么
slug: 穿越成了游戏里的炮灰角色
content_zh:
会议室里，马尔科僵在脸上的标准微笑只持续了几个呼吸。
他死死盯着坐在对面的那个戴着宽檐帽的男人。
那句“我现场给你做”
，像是一记重锤砸在他二十年的职业直觉上。
马尔科的瞳孔微微收缩，这还是他担任分行负责人以来，第一次在客户面前如此失态。
但马尔科毕竟是商行里摸爬滚打出来的老人。
他很快压下本能的震惊，用力清了清嗓子，将刚才差点脱手的烫金册子重新拿稳。
“先生，”
马尔科深吸了一口气，语调已经恢复了商人的口吻，甚至带上了一丝凌厉，“容我确认一下。
您的意思是，您可以现场制作足以达到暗拍准入标准的超凡物品？”
法伦微微点头，连眼皮都没有多抬一下。
马尔科沉默了一拍。
他那双精明的眼睛在法伦身上来回扫视，似乎想找出虚张声势的破绽，但他失败了。
他抬起手，打了个手势，示意身后的助手退出去，反手关上了会议室的门。
“既然如此。”
马尔科双手重新在桌上交叉，身子微微前倾，“我有一个提议。
赫本商行的材料库可以为您开放，制作所需的一切原料，由我们提供。”
他顿了顿，措辞变得严谨而冰冷，这是试探的第一步：“但规矩是规矩。
如果失败超过两次，消耗的材料费用需按市场价的三倍赔偿。
您接受吗？”

法伦没有任何犹豫：“可以。”
马尔科深深看了他一眼，拉开抽屉，抽出一张印有赫本商行防伪魔纹的羊皮契约纸。
他拿起桌上的钢笔，在条款栏里飞速填写了几行：赌约的内容、材料由商行提供、失败两次则三倍赔付。
填完后，他将契约推到法伦面前。
法伦拿起笔，行云流水地签下了字。
他没有用真名，落笔处只有一个笔锋凌厉、带着某种古老韵味的花体字母——“F”
“请随我来，”
马尔科站起身，深深鞠了一躬，“我带您去鉴定室。”
费尔明从椅子里像安了弹簧一样弹了起来，赶紧跟上。
他原本因为面对大商行负责人而发抖的腿，现在已经不抖了。
取而代之的是另一种紧张，或者说，是一种夹杂着战栗的兴奋。
……
鉴定室在商行的最深处，需要穿过一道依靠马尔科指纹的暗门。
房间内部的空间并不算大，但极为奢华。
四面墙上有三面嵌着从地板直通天花板的恒温材料架。
每一格都贴着精密防潮的标签，从普通的低阶魔兽皮底材，到封在水晶瓶里的高阶灵体残片，应有尽有，散发着五颜六色的微弱灵光。
房间中央，则是一张用整块沉香木打造的标准化工作台。
马尔科在门口站定。
他身后跟着两名员工，一个是年轻的学徒，怀里紧紧抱着记录簿；另一个是稍年长的鉴定师，正习惯性地推了推鼻梁上的单片辅助目镜。
“客人需要什么材料，直接从架上取即可。”
content_en:
In the conference room, Marco's standard smile froze on his face and only lasted a few breaths.
He stared intently at the man wearing a wide-brimmed hat sitting opposite.
The phrase "I'll do it for you on the spot"
, like a heavy hammer hitting his professional intuition of twenty years.
Marco's pupils shrank slightly. This was the first time since he became the head of the branch that he had lost his composure in front of customers.
But Marco is, after all, an old man who worked his way up through the business.
He quickly suppressed his instinctive shock, cleared his throat forcefully, and regained his grip on the gold-gilded booklet that he had almost let go of just now.
"Sir,"
Marco took a deep breath, and his tone returned to that of a businessman, even with a hint of sharpness, "Let me confirm.
You mean, you can make something on-site that's extraordinary enough to pass for dark shooting? "
Fallon nodded slightly without even raising his eyelids.
Marco was silent for a moment.
His shrewd eyes darted back and forth over Fallon, as if trying to find a flaw in his bravado, but he failed.
He raised his hand, gestured to the assistant behind him to exit, and closed the door of the conference room with his backhand.
"In that case."
Marco crossed his hands on the table again and leaned forward slightly, "I have a proposal.
The material library of Hepburn Company can be opened to you, and we provide all the raw materials needed for production. "
He paused, and his words became strict and cold, which was the first step of temptation: "But the rules are the rules.
If it fails more than twice, the cost of materials consumed must be compensated at three times the market price.
Do you accept it? "
Fallon said without any hesitation: "Okay."
Marco took a deep look at him, opened the drawer, and pulled out a piece of parchment contract paper printed with the anti-counterfeiting magic pattern of Hepburn Trading Company.
He picked up the pen on the table and quickly filled out a few lines in the terms column: the content and materials of the bet will be provided by the firm, and if it fails twice, the compensation will be tripled.
After filling it out, he pushed the contract in front of Fallon.
Fallon picked up the pen and signed it smoothly.
He did not use his real name, and there was only a sharp cursive letter with a certain ancient charm at the end of the pen - "F"
"Please come with me,"
Marco stood up and bowed deeply, "I will take you to the appraisal room."
Fermín jumped up from his chair like a spring and hurried to follow.
His legs, which were originally shaking when he was facing the person in charge of the big trading firm, stopped shaking now.
It was replaced by another kind of nervousness, or rather, a kind of excitement mixed with trembling.
…
The appraisal room is in the deepest part of the business house, and you need to go through a secret door that relies on Marco's fingerprints.
The space inside the room is not large, but it is extremely luxurious.
Three of the four walls are embedded with temperature-controlled material racks running from the floor to the ceiling.
Each grid is labeled with precision moisture-proof labels, ranging from ordinary low-level monster leather base materials to high-level spiritual body fragments sealed in crystal bottles, all exuding colorful and faint auras.
In the center of the room is a standardized workbench made of a single piece of agarwood.
Marco stopped at the door.
Behind him were two employees. One was a young apprentice, holding the record book tightly in his arms; the other was an older appraiser, who was habitually pushing the single-chip auxiliary eyepiece on the bridge of his nose.
“Whatever materials the customer needs, they can just take them directly from the shelf.”
